name: earshot
works_with: Claude Code and other MCP clients, plus a CLI and Python API
short: Lets a coding agent hear audio: describe a sound, find a moment in a recording, score a film's soundtrack, and make sound effects in code.
what: earshot turns sound into text an agent can reason about. It can say what a file sounds like, check how well it fits a description, find the best moment in a long recording, tell a real recording from a synthesized one, and score a launch film's sound against seven professional ones. It can also make sounds as code and improve them by listening, and it ships a bank of 201 sound effects. It runs locally on CPU as a CLI, a Python API and an MCP server.
who: People who use an agent to make videos, product demos or games in code and want the sound checked too. If you don't work with audio, skip it.
needs: ffmpeg and ffprobe on your PATH
About 1.1 GB of disk for two open models, downloaded on first use
A Gemini API key, only for the optional audio LLM critique

steps.title: Check the install
steps.text: Use `earshot doctor --fetch` if you want to download the models up front.

steps.title: Add it to your agent as an MCP server
steps.text: This is the Claude Code command. Change the path to where you cloned it. Other clients can use the same command in their `.mcp.json`.
steps.code: claude mcp add earshot --scope user -e EARSHOT_THREADS=3 -- /path/to/earshot/.venv/bin/python -m earshot mcp

steps.title: Add the AI skills (optional)
steps.text: Copy or symlink `skills/earshot` and `skills/real-sound` into `~/.claude/skills/` or a project's `.claude/skills/`.

watch: The first model use downloads about 1.1 GB into `.cache/hf` inside the repo. After that it loads from the cache and never contacts the Hub. Set `EARSHOT_OFFLINE=1` to block downloads.
Each CLI call loads the models first, which takes about 20 to 40 seconds. The MCP server keeps them loaded.
On a slow machine, start Claude Code with `MCP_TIMEOUT=60000`.
The `llm` command uploads audio to Gemini, and only runs with your own key and the `--yes-upload` flag.
The README's own limits: it can't judge taste, emotion, licences or speech content, and its critic can be pleased without the sound getting better. A human listen is still the final check.
The reference recordings for `--refset` are licensed and not in the repo. Bring your own with `--refs`.
